The Hidden Benefit Of Being Retired In A Bear Market

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1992 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As my public equity portfolio gets obliterated thanks to being overweight tech stocks, I started dusting off my resume to go back to flipping burgers at McDonald’s.
  • Recent findings suggest that as every long-time investor knows, the name of the game is survival.
  • Industry observers note that we're not in an official bear market, yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As my public equity portfolio gets obliterated thanks to being overweight tech stocks, I started dusting off my resume to go back to flipping burgers at McDonald’s. Then halfway through the application, I wiped away my tears and took a deep breath.

Recent findings suggest that as every long-time investor knows, the name of the game is survival. If you can make it through the downturn, good things usually await on the other side.

Industry observers note that we're not in an official bear market, yet. But plenty of individual tech names have already fallen by over 20%, and when you're overweight those names, the index's official status doesn't matter much.

Recent findings suggest that so I thought it might be helpful for those who are retired, or who are close, to discuss the positives of going through a downturn. We'll also review how long downturns usually last so we can better prepare.

As the midterm elections revealed, a lot of people are not happy with the way our country has been led. But the discontent didn't appear overnight. The stock market was simply acting as a giant dose of Lidocaine.

According to recent reports, as long as stocks kept going up, we could more easily bear higher oil prices, higher food prices, higher housing costs, higher college tuition costs, and explosive medical costs. After all, our investment returns were growing faster than inflation. $6 for a gallon of gas stings a lot less when your brokerage account is up $50,000 for the year.

Recent findings suggest that but that tolerance for rising costs disappears the moment our investments start losing money. Suddenly, $89 a pound for wagyu feels personal.

Recent findings suggest that when the wealth effect vanishes, consumers cut back. Fewer dinners out. Fewer vacations. The new car gets pushed out another year. With declining corporate profitability, companies accelerate layoffs to protect margins. The newly unemployed tighten spending even further.

Rinse and repeat until economists officially declare a recession six months after everybody already felt it.

It has been revealed that if you see the writing on the wall, you want want to get ahead of the layoffs by negotiating your own severance package. If you do, you will probably have an easier time getting a much better exit offer than being lumped with the masses.

Recent findings suggest that if you're newly retired, your biggest fear is sequence of returns risk. That's the risk of suffering massive losses early in retirement while you're also withdrawing money to live on. Do that for too long and your portfolio may never recover.

According to recent reports, lose enough and you get forced back to work. Nobody who has tasted freedom wants to return to Monday morning status meetings and performance reviews from someone half their age.

In a recent development, retirees who live off their investments should feel worse about a bear market more than the average worker. We don’t have a paycheck to cushion the blow. We may not have much spare cash flow to buy the dip either.

But here's the key point. If your investments can survive the correction or bear market, you should actually feel good during a downturn. Not ecstatic, but relatively good. Because the alternative is working hard for no financial reward.

Sources indicate that how do you know if you can survive? Run through this quick checklist:.

According to recent reports, so how long will the pain last? History offers some comfort, provided you have the patience of a parent waiting for a toddler to put on his shoes while already 15 minutes late.

Industry observers note that according to Capital Group, the S&P 500 has dropped 10% or more about once every 18 months since 1954. A 20%+ bear market shows up about once every six years.

Recent findings suggest that in other words, if you strategy on a 40-year retirement, expect roughly 25 corrections and six or seven bear markets. Declines are the price of admission, not a sign the world is ending. Get used to them.

Source: Capital Group, S&P 500 data from 1954 through 2025.

Industry observers note that hartford Funds, using Ned Davis Research data going back to 1928, counts 27 bear markets. Stocks fell 35% on average and took 289 days, or about 9.6 months, to hit bottom.

It has been revealed that bear markets were far more common during the Depression era. Since 1945, there have been 15, or one about every 5.1 years.

It has been revealed that two caveats before you get too comfortable. First, these figures measure peak to trough. Getting back to your old high takes longer. Second, the 1973 and 1980 bear markets each dragged on for more than 600 days. Averages are nice until you're living through the outlier.

But here's the part that should make everyone feel better. Every S&P 500 correction since 1929 has been followed by a recovery, and the average return in the first year after the bottom was 52%. And the recoveries are happening quicker now, if we include the 2025 Liberation Day and 2026 Iran War events.

In a recent development, hartford also found that about 42% of the S&P 500's strongest days over the past 20 years occurred during bear markets. Sell in a panic and you'll likely miss the rebound.

My takeaway: In a realistic worst-case scenario, plan on gutting out roughly 12 to 18 months of pain from peak to trough, with a longer tail to fully recover. That's why the one to two years of cash is fine, especially with interest rates still high.

The existential dilemma of a bear market is this:.

It has been revealed that the correct answer is to work less hard and YOLO more. Let me explain using a concept I call Return On Effort (ROE).

In a recent development, during a bull market, working less hard actually increases your Return On Effort because your investments provide most of the returns. Unless you have a sales job or some other role tightly correlated to performance, an extra 15 hours a week rarely moves the needle. You're better off riding the organization's growth.

During a bear market, working hard to run in place or lose money makes even less sense. There's nothing you can do to stem declining consumer confidence, new socialist policies, higher taxes, and so forth. Your boss isn't handing out raises while revenue is falling. See Google's collapse after having such a huge lead in the AI race.

If anything, your extra effort earns you the privilege of doing the work of three colleagues who just got laid off. Congratulations on your 0% raise.

In a recent development, so you work less hard to protect your declining Return On Effort. Not because you're lazy. Because you're rational.

With this logic in mind, who works the least? The unemployed, the traditional retiree, and the early retiree.

Therefore, so long as your investments can withstand the beating, you're going to be just fine. Psychologically, as a retiree, you must push yourself to do less and have more fun.

It has been revealed that happiness is relative. During a bull market, plenty of early retirees feel a twinge of FOMO watching former colleagues get promoted and cash fat RSU checks. During a bear market, that FOMO flips. Nobody envies the guy grinding through a reorg while his stock comp gets cut in half.

Whether you’re retired or still grinding away, a downturn offers some real perks.

1) Things get cheaper. When demand falls, so do prices for travel, hotels, and eventually real estate. Retirees with flexible schedules can travel off-peak and score deals that working parents can only dream about. Workers looking to buy their first home may finally face less competition.

Recent findings suggest that 2) You get to shop the sale. Retirees with passive income and a cash buffer get to buy when others are forced to sell. Workers get an even steadier advantage. Every paycheck and 401(k) contribution now picks up more shares at lower prices. Steady income plus a long time horizon makes you the natural buyer in a bear market.

3) Your kids get to buy the dip. I’ve written about how to use stock market downturns to make your kids millionaires. As a father, this is my favorite benefit of a bear market. Because the equity train finally stops long enough for kids to catch up and hop on board. A child has 50+ years of compounding ahead. A 30% drop today is a rounding error by the time they’re in their 50s.

Recent findings suggest that 4) Tax moves get better. Tax-loss harvesting offsets future gains. Roth conversions at depressed valuations mean you pay less tax on the same number of shares, and all the recovery happens tax-free.

In a recent development, 5) The AI hedge is doing its job. Public AI stocks have gotten crunched. But there’s a flip side. If AI companies are struggling to justify their valuations, AI probably isn’t wiping out white-collar work as fast as everyone feared. That’s comforting for our kids, and for every worker wondering if their job will exist in 10 years.

6) You get humbled and build resilience. Being heavily overweight tech felt brilliant for years. Bear markets remind us we’re not as smart as we thought. My advice after every huge win is to go scrub all your toilets. Every downturn you survive makes you a calmer, better investor for the next one. If you’re still working, just make sure your emergency fund is solid, because layoffs tend to show up at the worst time.

You can’t control tech volatility, interest rates, or who wins elections. But you can control how you spend your time during a downturn.

The market will eventually recover. It always has. When it does, the people who grinded through the downturn will be exhausted. Those of us who leaned into family, friends, and fitness will be well rested. Both groups will survive, which is what matters most.

If you’ve been thinking about retiring, a bear market may be the best time to pull the trigger. It means that in spite of the carnage, your finances are strong enough for you to break free. Waiting for the next bull market can feel safer, but it’s backwards.

Sources indicate that if your finances can support retirement while stocks are down 20% or more, your plan has already passed the stress test. You’re not retiring on inflated numbers that could vanish in the next correction. And since bear markets don’t last forever, a recovery may carry your retirement forward with a tailwind instead of a headwind.

According to recent reports, compare that to the person who retires at the peak of a bull market, only to watch their portfolio drop 30% in the first two years. That’s sequence of returns risk at its worst.

So go play in the park. Take your kids to the beach. A downturn is the best time to enjoy the freedom you worked so hard to build, and maybe the best time to claim it.

In a recent development, are you finding it more comforting to be retired during a downturn, or more stressful? How much of your portfolio would need to fall before you'd seriously consider going back to work? Do you agree that working less hard in a bear market is the rational move, or is that just a cop-out for the lazy? And for those still working, has the market selloff made you rethink how hard you're grinding? Are you using the downturn to fund your kids' investment accounts?

If you want a roadmap for getting through downturns and coming out richer, pick up a copy of Millionaire Milestones: Simple Steps To Seven Figures, a USA Today bestseller. It covers how to keep investing when everybody else is scared, so you can reach financial independence sooner.

In a recent development, robert Cowden and Enzo. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

In a recent development, when he left Latest Haven with Enzo, Cowden was at a low point. His battle with alcohol addiction had cost him his job, car, and home. Entering a residential treatment program would leave Enzo with no place to go. Now sober and with housing waiting for him after the end of his journey, Cowden sees his expedition as part of the larger effort to rebuild his life.

During the walking stage, Cowden towed his camping gear and supplies in a cart, which Enzo could ride in to take a break from walking. Setting out with very little, Cowden has relied on the kindness of strangers, both online and on the trail, to continue his expedition.

Industry observers note that “The number one warning you’re going to get on a walk across America is, ‘Be careful, there’s creepy people and bad people,'” Cowden recalled, speaking to a local KOMU 8 reporter while passing through Missouri. Industry observers note that cowden reveals the wear on his trail shoes, as Enzo looks on. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

While the second stage lets him and Enzo get off their feet, it has its own challenges. They launched the canoe into the Allegheny River at Pittsburgh. It soon joined the Ohio, and lengthy stretches of slow water pushed Cowden to paddle continuously.

It has been revealed that it’s 1,579km down the Ohio to its confluence with the Mississippi in Illinois, which Cowden and Enzo aim to complete in under 40 days. They’re currently on pace, averaging about 20km a day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most victims of animal attacks around the world are not tourists but the people who live amid potentially dangerous animals all the time. Here are some incidents from the last seven days.

A tiger killed two farmers in separate incidents about five kilometers apart within 24 hours in the eastern corner of India’s Maharashtra state.

According to recent reports, sixty-year-old farmer Nana Kambadi was killed by a tiger while working in his field on Saturday evening. The following evening, Premila Mahadole, 40, was attacked while harvesting rice. Her body was later found in the field. Officials suspect it was the same tiger, but this has not been confirmed.

Sources indicate that the back-to-back killings have thrown residents across the district into a panic, according to the Times of India. At this time of year, many are out in their fields harvesting rice at the edges of forests.

#33582. Loud Wealth vs. Stealth Wealth: Why Materialism Fades Over Time

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1458 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

Loud Wealth vs. Stealth Wealth: Why Materialism Fades Over Time

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1458 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I’m a proponent of stealth wealth.
  • It has been revealed that stealth wealth is also the natural endgame of following FIRE principles for decades.
  • So by default, every long-term FIRE practitioner eventually becomes a stealth wealth practitioner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I’m a proponent of stealth wealth. It makes for a more peaceful life with lower expectations and less scrutiny. The last thing you want to do is show off and put you and your family in danger.

It has been revealed that stealth wealth is also the natural endgame of following FIRE principles for decades. If you keep living well below your means, which is required to retire early, your investments will eventually compound faster than you can spend.

So by default, every long-term FIRE practitioner eventually becomes a stealth wealth practitioner. Whether they mean to or not.

It has been revealed that in private, you can do whatever you want. But in public, staying low-key is better. Here are three simple steps to follow:.

1) Dress simply. No designer brands or fancy outfits. Clean, comfortable clothes are all you need. Think jeans, t-shirt, warm jacket, sweater, sneakers, baseball hat.

2) Drive an old car. Driving a upcoming car is stressful and can attract unwanted attention. If you insist on a luxury brand, try to keep it for at least 10 years.

3) Stay quiet about your spending on social media. Don't post vacation photos or the nice things you buy. If a tree falls in Hawaii and nobody sees it on Instagram, did the vacation still happen? Yes, and it was more relaxing.

Do these three things and you’ll join the Stealth Wealth club, a group of operators who move in and out of the shadows unnoticed.

Industry observers note that once you’re in, you’ll realize there are far more members than you think. That realization is oddly bullish. A lot more people are doing better than the media or politicians would have you believe. They’re just not wearing it.

In 8th grade in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, I wanted two things: to be cool and to have girlfriends.

Sources indicate that my parents drove a 1976 Datsun with missing hubcaps. Getting dropped off in that car was social agony. So I had to find status elsewhere.

At the time, there were two ways to increase your coolness as a teenager: be a good skateboarder or dress in designer clothes. I chose both.

According to recent reports, I still remember forking over 160 ringgit, about $64 back then (roughly $150 today), for a used pair of Armani Exchange jeans. 30-inch waist, 31-inch cut length, bronze eagle triangle on the back pocket. That was an absurd amount of money for a 13-year-old to spend on pants. But all the cool rich kids had them, so I had to have them too.

Then came the equally expensive Doc Martens. Then a Guess shirt. Looking back, nearly all my work and allowance money went to clothes and shoes.

It has been revealed that and you know what? I enjoyed it. It made me feel good, and I was part of the cool crowd with plenty of friends.

In a recent development, today, I couldn’t give two shitake mushrooms about designer labels. I want comfortable, practical clothes with zipper pockets so I don’t lose my wallet, phone, and keys. I cut my own hair to save time and money, and I usually cover it with a frayed baseball cap anyway.

So what happened between Armani jeans and black running pants?

I stopped needing respect from everyone.

I’m writing this post because of a clip from author Min Jin Lee explaining why some people with little money spend lavishly on material things. As personal finance enthusiasts, we shake our heads at such conspicuous spending. Don’t they want to eventually be financially free? We think to ourselves. But we’re missing something important.

It has been revealed that her point: when you grow up in a poor community, respect matters enormously. It becomes a kind of currency. And when you don’t have much else, you tend to overvalue it. So you buy the nicer clothes, shoes, watches, and cars, hoping they command respect, even if it means carrying credit card debt.

This resonated with me as a minority who came to America for high school and faced various racist incidents. Racism is one of the deepest forms of disrespect because you're insulted just for being who you are. Respect, especially for elders, is a significant part of Asian culture. When people disrespect me online or in real life, it can be infuriating. In my younger years, I’d go after them to defend my honor.

When you think about it this way, materialism isn’t irrational. It’s a logical strategy for buying respect when you don’t have other ways to earn it. With this understanding, I'm going to try and be extra respectful to everybody I interact with from now on.

It has been revealed that at 13, I spent a fortune on Armani jeans to earn respect from my skater friends and the girls I liked. When I started working in finance, I dressed to earn respect from my peers and bosses.

According to recent reports, then I left finance in 2012. Overnight, the nice clothes went untouched. I no longer needed respect from anyone outside my home.

Funny enough, they're all still hanging in my closet 14 years later in pristine condition.

Sources indicate that today, insults from random folks feel more like pinches instead of body blows. The passive income is doing its job as a shield.

As a dad now, the only people I want respect from are my wife and children. Having respect from my parents and sister would be nice too, but we don’t see each other day-to-day so it’s no significant deal if not. As any parent and provider knows, taking care of a family is hard work.

As a result, on our family trip to Las Vegas, I confess that a part of me felt disrespected when my wife gave me a bothersome look when I asked her to take a few more profile photos of me at Redrocks.

Recent findings suggest that in that moment, my brain immediately pulled up the receipts. I agreed to this $7,000 trip despite being in a liquidity crunch. I went to bed at 2 am and still woke up by 6 am to get everyone breakfast. What’s the massive deal?

Yes, I realize feeling disrespected in that moment might sound ridiculous. But that’s the point. A man wants to feel respected by his wife and children he provides for.

Reaching FIRE doesn’t eliminate the desire for respect. It just shrinks the circle of people whose respect you care about. The flip side is that when you don’t get respect from the few people who matter most, it stings far more than any stranger’s opinion ever could.

It’s worth doing an honest self-assessment of your spending on material things.

According to recent reports, maybe you genuinely love watches, cars, clothes, shoes, jewelry, or handbags. That’s fine, as long as you can comfortably pay cash and never carry a revolving credit card balance.

But if you’re buying expensive things you don’t even use or love, you may still be chasing status to earn respect.

Sources indicate that maybe the midlife sports car is compensating for something. Maybe the designer wardrobe is a response to someone who once made an unkind comment about your body. Or maybe the nonstop social media highlight reel is an attempt to prove the middle school bullies wrong.

Whatever the reason, it’s worth exploring. Because the people you’re trying to impress are probably too busy trying to impress someone else. Know that there is an incredible joy of being a nobody so long as you have your finances in order.

For many of us in the FIRE community, the desire for stuff fades over time because the need for outside respect fades too. Once you’re living the life you want and own the things you need, strangers have nothing left to grant you. Nobody can hand you a better life than the one you’ve already built.

Recent findings suggest that that’s the real luxury of stealth wealth. Not hiding your money, but no longer needing an audience for it.

Sources indicate that readers, did you go through a loud wealth phase when you were younger? What was your version of the Armani jeans? Do you think materialism is really about respect, or is something else going on? And now that you’re older, whose respect do you still care about, and how do you feel when you don’t get it?

Stealth wealth means nobody else needs to know your net worth. But you should.

According to recent reports, people spend thousands on designer clothes to impress strangers. A free expert review of your finances is a far better flex, even if nobody sees it.

#33581. U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1106 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).
  • The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style.
  • On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).

The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style. They summited on October 20 and rode/skied down via the same line on the south face, while American photographer Blake Gordon and Canadian cinematographer Leo Hoorn filmed from a high camp.

On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026. Photo: Nick Russell.

“The south face of Dorje was always the goal, and I’d been planning/dreaming of it for over two years,” Nick Russell told ExplorersWeb while on his way to the airport.

The expedition reached base camp on October 6, shortly after an intense storm blanketed Nepal’s mountains with heavy snow. For them, however, the snow was a blessing rather than a curse.

“The cyclone gave our zone some much-needed snow down low, and on the face, it allowed a clean descent (no down climbing, no rappels),” Russell stated.

Sickness slowed the beginning of the expedition. “Three out of five of us, myself included, caught COVID,” Russell noted. Luckily, the climbers recovered just as the weather cleared and winds dropped, followed by a string of perfect days.

In a recent development, after the descent. Photo: Nick Russell/Instgram.

It has been revealed that “Adam, Billy, and I all carried our own gear, set the tracks, and climbed in alpine style on the face,” Nick Russell mentioned. The team had hired three Sherpa climbers (Dawa Geljee Sherpa, Kami Sherpa, and Nuri Sherpa) who helped the camera crew get their gear to a high camp, plus a base camp crew, outfitted by Shangri-La Nepal Trek.

Recent findings suggest that high camp at 6,000m on the south face of Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

In a recent development, the line of ascent/descent followed the snow from below 4,500m to Camp 1 (4,900m) by crossing an icefall. According to the team, this was the only real crux of the ascent, due to overhead serac hazard. At least, the exposed section was short — less than an hour.

Industry observers note that on the first day of the summit push, the team continued to their high camp at 6,000m, below the col and at the base of the snowy face. Russell recalls the details of the climb as follows:.

The south face is quite steep and sustained above the bergshrund, with sustained 45-50˚ and pockets of 55º, we estimate. The face had seen so much sun [over] the past two weeks that the rising conditions were the biggest unknown of the entire project.

It has been revealed that we didn’t know whether or not it would be too icy to ride/ski until we got on the face. The snow was mostly firm, pretty much on the brink of being edge-able. It was two tool and crampon climbing the entire way, with no proper rests to take the pack off.

It has been revealed that it took about 7.5 hours to climb the face, and we topped out around 1:30 pm. It took roughly 1.5 hours to descend, with breaks for the cameras to reset.

A climber leaves almost no tracks in the hard snow on Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

The three summiters started down from the top at the same time, Russell on snowboard and his partners on skis. It was anything but easy.

“The snow was more firm than I would have liked, but just edgeable enough to hold an edge,” Russell recalls. “Between the altitude, exposure below, steepness, and how firm it was, it was by far the heaviest line I’ve ever ridden.” He added that if the snow had been a little harder, they would have had to rappel down.

Recent findings suggest that the hard snow on the upper sections. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

“You always hope for stable, boot-top powder, but that’s rarely the case at high altitude,” Russell explained. “Instead, you make the most of the conditions presented and try to do it as safely as possible.”.

Sources indicate that he added: “The entire line was a no-fall zone; one lost edge, and it’d be over. Regardless of conditions, it was a dream for all of us to ride off the top of a peak in Nepal.”.

After a partial descent, the team spent the night at high camp, hoping to ride some interesting slopes they had spotted earlier, but finally decided to bail the next morning. “We were satisfied,” Russell remarked. They continued on skis/snowboard all the way down to the moraines below Camp 1 around 4,500m.

Childhood friends Fabrikant and Haas often partner up on major ski expeditions, mainly in Alaska but also in the Himalaya. They climbed and skied both Gasherbrums 1 and 2 without oxygen after climbing them in the same style in 2024, together with Brendan O’Neill.

“They are the strongest partners I’ve ever been in the mountains with,” said Russell, who has also climbed and snowboarded twice in the Indian Himalaya and twice in Nepal.

“I tried Dhaulagiri in 2022 with Blake Gordon and Dan Corn, but the difficult conditions that year coupled with the loss of Hilaree Nelson [who fell to her death while trying to ski down Manaslu] didn’t allow us to make very much progress,” Russell said.

“I’ve always dreamed of riding lines in the Himalaya, and this felt like a major step forward in my personal journey,” he concluded.

It has been revealed that while this is the first ski and snowboard descent of Dorje Lhakpa’s south face, the legendary Marco Siffredi snowboarded the west ridge of the mountain in 1999, with Bertrand Delapierre. Siffredi perished shortly afterward on the Hornbein Couloir on Mount Everest. “Dorje Lhakpa first entered my psyche from Marco and Bertrand’s descent,” the rider recalled.

The south face of Dorje Lhakpa was only climbed for the first time in 2021, by Spaniards Mikel Inoriza, Iker Madoz, and Mikel Zabalza.

“I came across a photo of the south face and the American Alpine Journal article from the Spanish team’s first ascent in 2021,” Russell remarked. “The massive south face is visible from the Kathmandu Valley on a clear day, and it is honestly crazy to me that no one had skied it before.”.

“Today,” he went on, “people are so hyper-focused on the 8,000m peaks (for good reason, I get it), but there are still virgin lines waiting for a snowboard/ski descent in the 6,000-7,000m range. It just takes a shit ton of work to make it happen.”.

Saddle to Paddle: Bikerafting From Canada to Mexico

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails.
  • According to recent reports, before starting the journey on September 17, he mentioned they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S. from Canada to Mexico. Starting in Glacier National Park, they will cross four rivers and six U.S. states to finish in El Paso, Texas.

According to recent reports, their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails. This allows the pair to cross landscapes that would usually require separate trips by bike and watercraft. Streufert, a geospatial wildfire scientist and cartographer, came up with the route by combining existing GPS tracks and geographical data from Bikepacking.com, American Whitewater, and OpenStreetMap. He overlaid cycling corridors and rivers to identify where the two could connect.

According to recent reports, before starting the journey on September 17, he mentioned they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes. So it is possible that they are the first to do so.

It has been revealed that they started what they neatly call the Saddle to Paddle Traverse on September 17, from Glacier National Park, Montana, on the Canadian border. They kicked off the first packrafting section with a 115km descent of the North Fork of the Flathead River, which forms part of the western boundary of Glacier National Park.

From there, they followed the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route through Montana toward Jackson Lake, Wyoming, for 1,107km. Here, they hit their second paddling phase on the Snake River.

It has been revealed that every time they reach a river, the pair inflates their rafts, load their bicycles aboard, and paddle downstream. Then at each takeout, they deflate the rafts, attach them to their bikes, and continue riding.

The route. Photo: Pete Streufert.

According to recent reports, after 130km along the Snake River, their route joined the SLoToJa cycling corridor. They pedaled through Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Here, a short connector track took them onto the newly developed Golden Gravel Trail. A further 860km of cycling brought them to Utah’s Green River.

They then paddled 328km through Desolation and Gray Canyons, including a handful of Class III rapids, and their only Class IV rapid of the trip.

Pulling their rafts out in Canyonlands National Park, they took the White Rim Trail to Moab. They are now taking a few days in Moab to “get all the mud off our bikes and escape the rain for a day or two before we keep heading south,” indicates Streufert.

From here, they will once again pick up the Golden Gravel Trail through the La Sal Mountains and across Colorado, then continue on the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route to Latest Mexico.

Recent findings suggest that paddling the Green River. Photo: Pete Streufert.

A final paddling section on Fresh Mexico’s Rio Chama will take them to the last leg of the trip, a 950km ride to El Paso.

The pair are riding Rodeo Labs Flaanimal 6.0 Steel, fitted with 29-inch Vittoria Mezcal tires, and using Kokopelli packrafts. The pair have described this as a “self-supported” route, although of course they’re replenishing their food along the way. They seem to combine camping with staying in towns.

View this post on Instagram See this post on Instagram.

Industry observers note that they should complete the journey within the next few weeks, within their two-month timeline. You can follow their progress here.

#33576. Breaking: Getting Rich Is Easy Compared To Finding And Keeping Love

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2263 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Getting Rich Is Easy Compared To Finding And Keeping Love

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.
  • It has been revealed that the first is economic stability.
  • Sources indicate that the second concern is bigger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.

It has been revealed that the first is economic stability. Will they be able to earn a livable wage in a world where AI keeps eating entry-level jobs? I question the time and money we spend educating our kids all the time. So I've been aggressively saving and investing for their future, just in case.

Sources indicate that the second concern is bigger. Will my children find love?

Recent findings suggest that A net worth target gets more achievable the more you save and the more time goes by. Compounding is boring, but it's reliable. If the direction is correct, sooner or later you will get there.

Finding a partner is far more amorphous. Our kids can work on their communication skills, fitness, charm, education, hygiene, empathy, and finances. But all of that merely improves their odds. There are no guarantees.

Which brings me to the strangest business story of 2026.

In a recent development, in late October, The New York Times reported that U.S. officials concluded a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a Chinese intelligence asset. She is a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center tech giant and Nvidia cloud partner that rents computing power to Chinese firms.

Surveillance of her reportedly revealed a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. And no, they are not related. Huang is a common surname like Smith.

The Financial Times then reported that a U.S. government memo described the relationship as romantic. Her alleged goal was to gather information on Jensen and advanced AI chips, and to nudge him to lobby for looser chip exports to China.

The allegations come from anonymous officials and haven't been tested publicly. Officials reportedly don't believe Jensen knew about any intelligence activity. Nvidia says his interactions with her were routine customer meetings. China denies the whole thing. House Republican committee chairs want a closed-door briefing on November 18.

So nobody outside the room knows the full story, except that Jensen admitted to the affair and is no longer CEO as of November 23, 2026. The lessons about love and money are worth discussing regardless of how the facts shake out.

Jensen Huang is worth over $120 billion (once $170 billion). He runs a manufacturer worth about $4 trillion after the sell-off. He is the closest thing we have to a modern-day emperor, the face of the AI revolution, mobbed like a rock star everywhere he goes in Taiwan.

And yet, if the reporting is accurate, it still wasn't enough.

In a recent development, there's a line from Gemma Teller Morrow in the TV show, Sons of Anarchy: “Only men need to be loved, sweetheart. Women need to be wanted.”.

Sources indicate that it's not entirely true. Everybody wants to be loved and desired to some degree. But the line points to something uncomfortable. No amount of money, applause, or leather jackets fills the need to feel admired by one specific person who seems to see you.

We all just want to be loved and accepted for who we are.

Here's the twist that makes this story sadder.

If U.S. officials are right, what may have felt like admiration was tradecraft. Attentiveness, respect, and flattery are exactly what an intelligence service would deploy against the most important man in AI. Intelligence services have used romance as an opening for as long as there have been secrets worth stealing.

According to recent reports, which exposes the hidden problem of extreme wealth and power. The richer you get, the harder it becomes to know whether anyone loves you for you. Every new person in your life has a reason to be nice to you. Normal people get to skip that existential headache.

Money doesn't make finding love easier. Past a certain point, it makes find true love harder.

The people worth keeping are the ones who liked you before you were worth liking.

Jensen is far from the first emperor to create a commotion over love for a woman.

Paris and Helen of Troy. The Greeks' foundational story is about a prince who ran off with another man's wife and got his entire city burned to the ground. Myth, sure. But the Greeks clearly understood the risk.

Mark Antony and Cleopatra. Antony controlled half the Roman world. He chose Cleopatra over Rome, lost at Actium in 31 BC, and both were dead within a year. Octavian got the empire.

King Edward VIII. In 1936, he abdicated the British throne after less than a year to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American. He traded a kingdom for love, and spent the rest of his life in comfortable, irrelevant exile.

In a recent development, john Profumo. The closest parallel to the Jensen story. In 1963, Britain's Secretary of State for War was revealed to have had an affair with Christine Keeler, who was also involved with a Soviet naval attaché. Profumo lied to Parliament, resigned in disgrace, and the scandal helped bring down the government.

Recent findings suggest that brian Krzanich. Intel's CEO resigned in 2018 after a past consensual relationship with an employee came to light. Running a chip giant doesn't come with an exemption.

Jeff Bezos. His 2019 divorce after 25 years of marriage sent roughly 4% of Amazon, worth about $38 billion at the time, to MacKenzie Scott. Bezos kept his job, married Lauren Sánchez, and is still one of the richest men alive. But it was the most expensive breakup in history.

The pattern is clear. Kingdoms, careers, and fortunes are rebuildable. However, once you find the one, you will do anything to get them.

According to recent reports, remember Indecent Proposal from 1993? Robert Redford’s billionaire character offers a struggling couple, played by Demi Moore and Woody Harrelson, $1 million for one night with the wife. They take the deal. Their marriage nearly implodes.

Recent findings suggest that the couple discovered they had a price, and it wasn’t that high. But they badly underestimated what they were selling.

Meanwhile, the billionaire could buy the night. He couldn’t buy her heart. He had everything except the one thing he actually wanted.

Swap Redford for any modern tech billionaire and the lesson holds. Money can buy almost anything. Except the feeling of being genuinely loved.

The lack of money is a solvable problem.

Plenty of regular people have become millionaires this way. The formula is public.

Sources indicate that there is no formula for love. You can do everything right and still never meet the one. And even if you do, roughly 40% of first marriages in America end in divorce. Finding love involves tremendous luck. Keeping it is work.

It has been revealed that you can always make another dollar. You can't always make another soulmate.

In a recent development, in 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General declared loneliness an epidemic. About half of American adults report feeling lonely, and the health impact of social disconnection was compared to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.

The FIRE crowd isn't immune. Early retirement can be isolating. Your friends are at work. Your identity is gone. And if you're married, there's a specific trap worth sharing.

It has been revealed that FIRE is better when both partners retire and experience freedom together. Not when one spouse is slaving away while the other is kicking back. Resentment will surely kick in.

Yes, I get it. Some men’s egos still need protecting when their wives are bringing home the sashimi. But men need to get over themselves. Women now make up the majority of college students, and plenty of them will out-earn their husbands.

I left banking in 2012. My wife kept working until 2015 when she negotiated her own severance. For almost three years, I was the guy at home while she commuted.

If you're planning FIRE, proposal a joint exit. Life is better this way.

It has been revealed that 1) A high-value spouse may need more respect just to break even. If your partner is successful, attractive, or powerful, the world is constantly praising them. Next to all that adoration, treating them normally at home can inadvertently feel like a lack of respect, or even disrespect. So you may have to deliberately show more appreciation than feels natural just to run in place.

It has been revealed that 2) Everything gets taken for granted. Eat Kobe beef every day and you’ll get sick of it. In FIRE land, wake up without an alarm clock every day and you’ll take that for granted too. The antidote is voluntary discomfort. Scrub your own toilets after a big investment win. Take a part-time consulting gig a 40-minute bus ride away that makes you take orders from a micromanager. Practice fasting for at least 18 hours once a month if you have access to unlimited food. Doing uncomfortable things on purpose helps you appreciate the people you already have.

3) Privacy is priceless. When you’re private, you can fix your mistakes without the whole world watching. Being known in your small circle for something good is great. Being famous means millions of strangers have opinions about who you are. Respond to all of them and you’ll never have peace of mind. Embrace being a rich nobody.

Recent findings suggest that whatever the full truth turns out to be, this whole situation is sad. Sad for Lori and their adult children. Sad for Jensen and his legacy. Disappointing for Nvidia’s tens of thousands of employees and shareholders like me. And a blow for America, given we’re in a global AI race.

Relationships are hard. They require constant work and attentiveness. Forty years of marriage doesn’t buy you immunity. If anything, it makes it easier to stop paying attention.

If there’s one silver lining, it’s that this story may help bring the left and the right together on maintaining our lead in AI. AI spending has been one of the biggest drivers of U.S. economic growth. If post-midterm infighting causes us to lose the race, we could sink the economy along with it.

In a recent development, if someone with that much money and goodwill was allegedly willing to risk throwing it away, you can’t really blame people for their emotions and their desire to be loved. We’re all human.

Besides a basic amount of financial security, I hope my kids will find someone who will support, love, and cherish them. I would rather my kids find that person than be rich.

Recent findings suggest that money can help protect them after I’m gone. But money can’t hug them after a bad day, sit with them in a hospital waiting room, or celebrate their wins with them. Knowing they each have someone like that is what will let me rest easy. That’s when I’ll know my kids will be OK.

Then I hope they never take that person for granted. Because the odds say they will, just like most of us take for granted the water we drink and the air we breathe.

Industry observers note that readers, do you agree that making money is easier than finding love? Would you take the $1 million in Indecent Proposal, or $2.2 million in today's dollars? If you've achieved FIRE, did you and your spouse exit together, or did one of you keep working, and how did that affect your relationship? And if you had $140+ billion, how would you ever know if someone loved you for you?

If you're a worried parent, I'm diligently working on my new book out in Fall 2027, Your Kids Will Be OK: Smart Money Decisions For Parents In An Uncertain World, published by Portfolio Penguin. It's about raising capable, resilient kids and making solid money decisions so they have a real shot at independence, and at a good life.

In a recent development, you can’t buy love, but you can protect it. If your family depends on your income, term life insurance is one of the most loving financial moves you can make.

My wife and I each got matching 20-year term policies through Policygenius after shopping around for months. It took far less time than I expected, and we sleep better knowing our kids would be OK if the unthinkable happened. Check out Policygenius to compare quotes from top insurers for free.

Stocks can swing 20% on a single headline. Real estate tends to move more slowly, generate rental income, and give you something tangible to own. That’s why real estate has been a core part of my net worth for over 23 years, and it helps me sleep better when the stock market gets volatile.

It has been revealed that if you want real estate exposure without the hassle of being a landlord, check out Fundrise. It invests in a diversified portfolio of private real estate across the Sunbelt, including residential and industrial properties, and is expanding into data centers as demand for computing power grows. You can start with just $10.

In a recent development, money is the easier problem to solve, and I’ve been helping readers solve it since 2009. Join 60,000+ others and get my free weekly newsletter here. I share what I’m seeing and doing with my own money, plus the lessons on family, freedom, and life that don’t fit neatly into a spreadsheet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu.
  • According to recent reports, joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass.
  • Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu. He is recovering in intensive care. By law, all foreign trekkers are supposed to have a guide in the Khumbu.

According to recent reports, joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass. He was first taken to Lobuche, then flown out on October 27, according to The Tourism Times.

Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit. It links the Chhukung side of the Imja Valley with Lobuche over rocky, non-glaciated moraine. The crossing is long and remote; the descent toward Lobuche is often loose underfoot and comes after hours already spent at altitude.

The case has again drawn attention to Nepal’s rules in the Khumbu. Since 2023, the Nepal Tourism Board has required that all foreign trekkers be accompanied by a licensed guide within national parks, including Sagarmatha.

Recent findings suggest that in practice, the local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality has continued to issue its own permits and has not strictly enforced the national guide requirement. Thus, independent trekking remains common on the main Everest routes. Officials quoted by The Tourism Times described unguided travel in the region as a violation of the mandatory rule and a source of preventable rescues.

Cherubino was traveling alone when he was found. No further details on the circumstances of the fall or his condition have been released beyond the hospital’s assessment that he is recovering.

#33569. Baselane Review: How to Stop Landlord Burnout From Costing You $800,000+

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2477 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

Baselane Review: How to Stop Landlord Burnout From Costing You $800,000+

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rental property is how I broke free.
  • I’ve had good tenants, great tenants, and tenants who refused to take their trash with them during the final walkthrough.
  • Recent findings suggest that I’m forever grateful for owning rental property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rental property is how I broke free. The rent from my San Francisco properties was one of the foundations that let me leave banking in 2012 at age 34. Without it, I’d probably still be waking up at 5 am to get to the office by 5:45 am and leaving after 6 pm.

I’ve been a landlord since 2005. I’ve had good tenants, great tenants, and tenants who refused to take their trash with them during the final walkthrough.

Recent findings suggest that I’m forever grateful for owning rental property. But the older I get, the less I enjoy being a landlord.

It’s not the math. It’s the tenant headaches, the turnover, and the maintenance. The 9 pm leaky faucet text. The final walkthrough that starts 30 minutes late. At 49 with two young kids, my time is worth more and my patience is worth less.

2025 tested me with three tenant turnovers. Each one meant a deposit to return, walls to paint, a vacancy to absorb, and a newly introduced tenant to find. Not long after, I sold one of my rentals. Earning 100% passive income feels better.

Recent findings suggest that but selling also feels like giving up. Owning rental property is a war of attrition. The longer you hold, the more wealth you usually build. Hold until you pass, and your heirs may get a step-up in basis that wipes out the capital gains entirely.

Industry observers note that selling isn’t free either. Commissions, transfer taxes, capital gains, and depreciation recapture take a massive bite. Then you lose the rent check and future appreciation on a property you’ll likely never buy back at the same price.

Semi-passive income you can live with beats optimized income you can’t wait to dump. You can’t automate away a difficult tenant or a burst pipe. But you can automate a lot of what surrounds them. That’s where Baselane comes in.

For 21 years, I’ve tracked my rental finances with a spreadsheet and emails. Old school. With three rentals left in San Francisco, it kind of works. I know my numbers, more or less.

Recent findings suggest that but add another property, an LLC, a partner, or a short-term rental, and a DIY system starts to creak. Debits and credits slip through the cracks.

Industry observers note that four rentals is why I sold one last year. I couldn’t comfortably handle all the maintenance and management myself. And I didn’t want to pay a property manager 10% of rent or more to do a worse job than me.

According to recent reports, since Baselane is sponsoring this post, I opened a free account for one of my SF rentals to see how it compares. Here’s what stood out.

Baselane is a free business bank account, bookkeeping software, and rent collection app rolled into one login, built for landlords. Think business checking plus QuickBooks plus Venmo for rent, except it knows what a Schedule E is.

It has been revealed that banking and books live in the same system, so you never reconcile. Baselane is a fintech, not a bank. Deposits are held at Thread Bank, Member FDIC.

One of the first rules of landlording is to keep rental money separate from personal money. One of the second rules is that it gets messy fast once you own more than one property.

It has been revealed that with Baselane, you can open unlimited checking and savings accounts under one login. One per property, one per LLC, one for reserves, however you actually run your portfolio. There are no monthly maintenance fees and no minimum balances, which matters once you're running a handful of accounts.

It has been revealed that you can also issue physical and virtual debit cards with spending limits. If you pay contractors, cleaners, or a handyman, you can hand someone a card capped at, say, $1,500 for materials instead of fronting cash and chasing receipts.

Sources indicate that the reserve accounts earn interest. At the moment 2.88%. Letting a five-figure repair reserve sit in a checking account earning nothing is a donation to your bank.

Recent findings suggest that if you try it, start with one property. Move its rent and its bills over, get comfortable, then decide about the rest.

Plenty of banks let you open separate accounts. What's different here is that every transaction gets tagged to a property and a Schedule E category as it happens.

According to recent reports, here's why that matters. Before my old Marina tenants moved in, I spent about $2,500 and many hours fixing up the yard. They agreed to hire a gardener twice a month. They never did. Before they moved out, I paid my landscaper $1,400 including materials to restore it, plus two days of my own labor.

Industry observers note that those are deductible repair and maintenance expenses. But only if you record them against the right property and can find the receipts a year later. With one property, I can do that myself. With five, it becomes a part-time job.

Industry observers note that on the Smart strategy, you set rules once, like “payments to my landscaper go to the SF rental under Repairs,” and an AI assistant handles the rest. You can snap a photo of a receipt and it matches it to the transaction.

It has been revealed that this is the part that speaks to my real pain point: tenant headaches. It is also my favorite reason for using Baselane.

According to recent reports, I rented my Marina house to five tenants from 2015 to 2017 for about $8,200 a month. The lease charged a $250 late fee after the 4th. Rent was late eight times in 24 months. I waived the fee every single time.

That’s $2,000 I left on the table because I’m a softie who dislikes confrontation. Their method of paying was walking into my bank branch and depositing directly into my account. One July 4th weekend, rent revealed up on the 10th. That’s difficult to deal with when my mortgage is due by the 5th of each month, resulting in cash flow issues.

That awkwardness wore me down. In 2017, I sold the Marina house for about $2.75 million to simplify my life.

In a recent development, thanks to the AI boom pushing San Francisco prices higher, that house is likely worth $800,000 to $1 million more today. Sure, I reinvested the proceeds, so the true opportunity cost is lower. But it still stings.

Industry observers note that if I’d had a system to collect rent, send reminders, and enforce late fees without me playing bad cop, I would have held on. Selling out of fatigue can be one of the most expensive decisions a landlord makes.

That’s what Baselane does. Invoices, reminders, and late fees go out on schedule. Tenants can pay by ACH or card and set up autopay. Software doesn’t feel guilty enforcing a lease you both signed. Ultimately, Baselane removes friction which increases a rental property owner’s ability to hold on and build more wealth.

After 21 years, I've also learned that 99% of tenants want as little contact with their landlord as possible. The feeling is mutual. A system that runs rent in the background means fewer awkward conversations, and fewer awkward conversations means a happier landlord who's less tempted to sell.

It has been revealed that two catches. Tenants who pay by card pay a 3.49% fee, so steer them to ACH. And if your current rent collection works fine, then great. Baselane's value is rent, banking, and books living in one place.

If you run short-term rentals, payouts from Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com can take several business days to clear at a normal bank. Across multiple listings, that's a constant gap between money earned and money available.

Baselane offers faster payouts when you use it as your deposit account on booking platforms, with each listing feeding its own account. Next-day payouts are available for free consumers.

A healthy bank balance doesn't mean a property is performing. You might have a massive repair coming, insurance up 20%, or expenses sitting in the wrong account.

It has been revealed that I recently ran the numbers on my San Francisco rental for a post on whether to raise the rent when tenants strike it rich. Rent is $10,250 a month, roughly $1,250 below market, because I honor a three-year rent schedule capped at about 3% a year. One vacant month wipes out about eight months of that discount. And a 2.5% annual increase only covers about 80% of my rising insurance and basic maintenance costs.

Sources indicate that I know those numbers because I track them myself. Most landlords never sit down and run them.

Baselane builds income, expense, cash flow, and net operating income reports for each property or your whole portfolio, because every transaction is already tagged. No building spreadsheets from scratch.

It has been revealed that with one rental and a spreadsheet you trust, you may not need this. With several properties or LLCs, it's the difference between knowing and guessing whether a property is worth keeping.

Tax season is where sloppy books come back to bite. You end up gathering records, digging up receipts, and trying to remember what a charge from eight months ago was for.

Because Baselane categorizes everything during the year, you can download a tax package with Schedule E reports, income statements, and transaction ledgers with receipts for each property and entity. Then you hand it to your CPA or use it to file yourself.

Sources indicate that if you have one rental and a DIY system that works, you don't need it. But the Core plan is free, so there's little downside to trying it.

Industry observers note that baselane makes the most sense if you own several rentals, hold properties in LLCs, or self-manage. Property managers have quoted me fees ranging from 10% to 20% of rent. On a $10,250 rental, a 10% fee is $1,250 a month. Baselane Smart, its premium version is just $20.

That's not apples to apples. Baselane won't fix your garbage disposal or talk to your tenants. But if you self-manage, the administrative half of the job gets a lot lighter.

It's also worth a look if you're on the fence about selling a rental because you're worn out. Lighten the load before you list it and pay all those exorbitant fees. And if you're buying your next property, set up clean systems first. They're easier to build with one property than to retrofit with five.

Core is free and includes unlimited accounts, debit cards with spend controls, rent collection with automated reminders and late fees, property-level tracking, and the accountant tax package.

Smart is $20 a month with a 30-day free trial and adds AI auto-tagging, receipt matching, auto-transfers to maintain target balances, faster rent deposits, and balance sheet reports.

Compare that to what you may already pay. Some business bank accounts charge $5 to $25 a month in maintenance fees. At $15 a month across five accounts, that's $900 a year just to keep them open. Baselane charges no maintenance fees, no minimums, and ACH transfers and incoming wires are free.

No product is perfect, and pretending otherwise insults your intelligence.

Recent findings suggest that rental property helped me break free due to the semi-passive income it generates. But a rental only builds wealth if you can stand to keep owning it.

Industry observers note that the headaches that make me want to sell are tenants, turnover, and maintenance. Baselane doesn't make those entirely disappear. What it does is take the money side of landlording, rent collection, late fees, accounts, and records, and put it on autopilot. Less friction overall means more energy for the parts that actually need a human.

According to recent reports, my plan going forward is simple. Own fewer, better rentals and make each one as close to passive as possible. Let the private real estate side of my portfolio be 100% passive. And spend the time I save being a full-time dad.

Sources indicate that if I’d had automated rent and late fees with my Marina tenants, I’d have $2,000 more and far fewer awkward conversations. I also might still own the house today. That’s at least an $800,000 lesson in letting small annoyances drive significant decisions.

Recent findings suggest that selling a rental is permanent. Making one easier to own isn't.

If you own rental property and want it to feel a little more passive, check out Baselane here. The Core plan is free, so the only cost of trying it is an afternoon.

Have you ever sold a rental property because you were tired of managing it, not because the numbers stopped working? Do you regret it? What's the one landlord headache that would push you to sell: tenants, turnover, maintenance, or the paperwork? Do you track your rental finances yourself or hand them off? And have you ever waived a late fee you were fully entitled to collect?

What should real estate investors look for when choosing a bank? Look for property-specific accounts, integrated rent collection, automated bookkeeping, and tax prep support. Multi-property investors benefit most from platforms that organize transactions by property and entity automatically. Security deposit tracking also helps keep tenant funds clearly separated.

Recent findings suggest that can real estate investors open a business bank account online? Yes. Digital platforms like Baselane let you open accounts entirely online with no branch visit. Traditional banks may require in-person verification depending on their policies and your business structure.

Do any banking platforms for real estate investors offer high-yield savings? Digital-first platforms generally pay more on savings than traditional banks. Baselane pays a tiered APY on savings balances that exceeds the national average for business accounts. Traditional banks typically pay far less on business savings.

It has been revealed that how do integrated banking and bookkeeping platforms help with taxes? Platforms like Baselane categorize transactions by property and IRS Schedule E category throughout the year. That cuts manual work at tax time and produces Schedule E reports and transaction ledgers you can hand to your accountant or use to file yourself.

Does Baselane support multiple properties? Yes. Baselane supports bookkeeping across multiple rental properties for U.S.-based entities, including single-member and multi-member LLCs, corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships. Banking and rent collection sync directly with bookkeeping, and you can connect external bank accounts and import historical transactions. See the pricing page for the full feature list.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

West Ridge or Hornbein Couloir? Everest Team Prepares for Fourth Attempt

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time.
  • Andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening.
  • In a recent development, everest West Ridge some days ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time. While no easy option exists, they want to avoid the extremely exposed, difficult, and uncertain ridge route. Their only alternative is the Hornbein Couloir, which would force them to stray temporarily into Tibet.

Andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening. They will return to their base in Lobuche this weekend, determined to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen.

In a recent development, everest West Ridge some days ago. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Sources indicate that “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb. “Part of this time was spent exploring different options for accessing the route.”.

The Russian team has a permit to climb Everest from Nepal, as long as they attempt a route other than the standard Khumbu Icefall-South Col-Southeast Ridge. This has become the normal South Side route since Hillary and Tenzing’s first ascent in 1953.

Topo of the Russian team’s planned route on Everest, courtesy of Andrei Vasiliev.

Industry observers note that first, the Russians tried to bypass the Khumbu Icefall via the Nuptse Shoulder toward Camp 1, but heavy snow forced them to find another route. Crossing the Icefall (sharing paths with the normal route) was also too hard in the deep snow and on the shaky snow bridges over the innumerable crevasses.

Industry observers note that “Eventually, we selected a third option, via the Lho La,” Vasiliev said. “From that pass, our planned route continues across the West Shoulder, along the West Ridge.”.

According to recent reports, at the Lho La col. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

On their latest foray, the team reached 6,400m. “We climbed approximately twelve 60m pitches over rock, snow, and ice of moderate difficulty,” noted Vasiliev.

He noted that on the way to the West Shoulder, they found traces of previous expeditions, including old ropes and snow anchors.

As for the terrain ahead of them, Vasiliev said:.

From our highest point reached, the terrain ahead looks manageable. We can see two more steep rock steps, each approximately 100m high, along with possible bypasses on steep snow slopes. Beyond these obstacles, the terrain appears easier, and we hope to be able to move simultaneously.

Industry observers note that rocky section on the way to Everest’s West Ridge. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Vasiliev and his team are confident they can manage this route, despite doing so in increasingly wintry conditions.

In a recent development, the route linking the Lho La, the West Shoulder, and the West Ridge of Everest has been completed only twice. A Yugoslavian team led by Tone Skarja did the first complete ascent in 1979. They used the Hornbein Couloir variation on their descent.

According to recent reports, the only repetition was done by a Bulgarian team in 1984. Hristo Prodanov reached the summit on his own and retraced his steps down the ridge but never made it back alive. Some of his partners who summited days later descended via the normal route. Three other teams who climbed the West Shoulder-West Ridge summited by traversing to the North Face, on the Chinese side, and climbing the Hornbein Couloir.

It has been revealed that the North Face of Everest from the West Shoulder. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

In a recent development, objectively speaking, the Hornbein Couloir offers more summit (and survival) chances than the upper part of the West Ridge. However, it requires traversing into Chinese territory. The Russian team has a permit to climb only from Nepal. It is unclear if a brief border trespass could be considered, and Vasiliev has not confirmed what they will do. “First we need to complete one more rotation,” he remarked.
